```{r read in, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# based on explorative analysis, we are exploring acceleration, deceleration in relation with amplitude envelope and F0
```

For acceleration/deceleration, we need to multiply the data in order to get informative units. We multiply by a 100 to go from meters to centimeters. We multiply by 200 to compensate for the sampling rate (200Hz), so that we yield cm/s^2
Through this modification, we get information in cm/s^2.

```{r multiplication, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
f0_acc$wrist_apeak <- f0_acc$wrist_apeak*100*200
f0_dec$wrist_decpeak <- f0_dec$wrist_decpeak*100*200
env_acc$wrist_apeak <- env_acc$wrist_apeak*100*200
env_dec$wrist_decpeak <- env_dec$wrist_decpeak*100*200

```

We also normalize amplitude envelope peak in respective datasets
```{r envelope normalization, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

env_dec$wrist_envpeak_dec_norm <- NA
env_dec$wrist_envpeak_dec_norm <- ave(env_dec$wrist_envpeak_dec, env_dec$speaker, FUN = function(x) scale(x, center = FALSE, scale = TRUE)) 

env_acc$wrist_envpeak_acc_norm <- NA
env_acc$wrist_envpeak_acc_norm <- ave(env_acc$wrist_envpeak_acc, env_acc$speaker, FUN = function(x) scale(x, center = FALSE, scale = TRUE)) 

```


Remove the outliers according to Tukey's 1.5 IQR rule. This code should be run in the console, because the function prompts the user to answer whether they wish to remove the outliers or not.

```{r outliers, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Function
#source("http://goo.gl/UUyEzD")
outlierKD <- function(dt, var) {
     var_name <- eval(substitute(var),eval(dt))
     na1 <- sum(is.na(var_name))
     m1 <- mean(var_name, na.rm = T)
     par(mfrow=c(2, 2), oma=c(0,0,3,0))
     boxplot(var_name, main="With outliers")
     hist(var_name, main="With outliers", xlab=NA, ylab=NA)
     outlier <- boxplot.stats(var_name)$out
     mo <- mean(outlier)
     var_name <- ifelse(var_name %in% outlier, NA, var_name)
     boxplot(var_name, main="Without outliers")
     hist(var_name, main="Without outliers", xlab=NA, ylab=NA)
     title("Outlier Check", outer=TRUE)
     na2 <- sum(is.na(var_name))
     cat("Outliers identified:", na2 - na1, "n")
     cat("Propotion (%) of outliers:", round((na2 - na1) / sum(!is.na(var_name))*100, 1), "n")
     cat("Mean of the outliers:", round(mo, 2), "n")
     m2 <- mean(var_name, na.rm = T)
     cat("Mean without removing outliers:", round(m1, 2), "n")
     cat("Mean if we remove outliers:", round(m2, 2), "n")
     response <- readline(prompt="Do you want to remove outliers and to replace with NA? [yes/no]: ")
     if(response == "y" | response == "yes"){
          dt[as.character(substitute(var))] <- invisible(var_name)
          assign(as.character(as.list(match.call())$dt), dt, envir = .GlobalEnv)
          cat("Outliers successfully removed", "n")
          return(invisible(dt))
     } else{
          cat("Nothing changed", "n")
          return(invisible(var_name))
     }
}
```

# Modeling

## F0 Acceleration

### Preparation

Check for normality of the outcome variable: F0 peak nearest to acceleration peak.

```{r f0 acc normality, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# This distribution, especially the red line will be the one we will later see in the posterior predictive checks as y
hist(f0_acc$wrist_f0peak_acc, freq = FALSE, main = "Density curve")
lines(density(na.omit(f0_acc$wrist_f0peak_acc)), lwd = 2, col = 'red')

qqnorm(f0_acc$wrist_f0peak_acc)
qqline(f0_acc$wrist_f0peak_acc)

shapiro.test(f0_acc$wrist_f0peak_acc)

ks.test(f0_acc$wrist_f0peak_acc, 'pnorm')
```

The outcome variable is not normally distributed.

Now, let's check for correlation between speech rate and wrist acceleration peak. We use two methods: Bayesian and frequentist.

```{r f0 acc correlations, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Bayes factor
f0acc_corr_s <- correlationBF(f0_acc$speech_rate_s, f0_acc$wrist_apeak)
describe_posterior(f0acc_corr_s)
bayesfactor(f0acc_corr_s)

# Frequentist Kendall
cor(f0_acc$speech_rate_s, f0_acc$wrist_apeak)
cor.test(f0_acc$speech_rate_s, f0_acc$wrist_apeak,  method="kendall")

```

Bayes factor points to a very strong evidence for a correlation.

We set weakly informative priors. We truncate the intercept prior to include only positive values, with the lowest point to be 70 Hz. Any lower values would be erroneous octave jumps and they were discarded in the pre-processing.

```{r f0 acc priors, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
get_prior(
  wrist_f0peak_acc ~ 1 +
    speech_rate_s +
    point_direct_s +
    wrist_apeak +
    sex_s +
    point_direct_s * wrist_apeak +
    (1 | speaker) +
    (0 + speech_rate_s + point_direct_s + wrist_apeak + point_direct_s * wrist_apeak | speaker) +
    (1 | rhyme) +
    (0 + speech_rate_s + point_direct_s + wrist_apeak + sex_s + point_direct_s * wrist_apeak | rhyme),
  data = f0_acc,
  family = "gaussian"
)

prior1 <- set_prior("truncated_normal(0, 200, lower = 70)", class = "Intercept")
prior2 <- set_prior("normal(0, 75)", class = "b", coef = "sex_s")
prior3 <- set_prior("normal(0, 10)", class = "b", coef = "point_direct_s")
prior4 <- set_prior("normal(0, 1)", class = "b", coef = "point_direct_s:wrist_apeak")
prior5 <- set_prior("normal(0, 10)", class = "b", coef = "speech_rate_s")
prior6 <- set_prior("normal(0, 1)", class = "b", coef = "wrist_apeak")
prior7 <- set_prior("normal(0, 100)", class = "sd")
prior8 <- set_prior("normal(0, 100)", class = "sigma")
prior9 <- set_prior("lkj(2)", class = "cor")
priors_f0_acc <- list(prior1, prior2, prior3, prior4, prior5, prior6, prior7, prior8, prior9)
priors_f0_acc <- prior_summary(priors_f0_acc)


```

### Gaussian + priors

This is the model code.

```{r f0 acc model, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

f0peak_acc <- brm(
  wrist_f0peak_acc ~ 1 +
    speech_rate_s +
    point_direct_s +
    wrist_apeak +
    sex_s +
    point_direct_s * wrist_apeak +
    (1 | speaker) +
    (0 + speech_rate_s + point_direct_s + wrist_apeak + point_direct_s * wrist_apeak || speaker) +
    (1 | rhyme) +
    (0 + speech_rate_s + point_direct_s + wrist_apeak + sex_s + point_direct_s * wrist_apeak || rhyme),
  data = f0_acc,
  family = "gaussian",
  prior = priors_f0_acc,
  # Technical stuff
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  # Number of chains
  chains = 4, 
  # Number of iterations per chain
  iter = 10000,
  warmup = 2000,
  # Number of cores to use
  cores = 4,
  # Seed for replicability
  seed = 123,
  # Convergence
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
  # Save here
  file = paste0(parentfolder, "/9_statistical_analysis_scripts_and_model_output/f0peak_acc_new.rds"))

```

Load ready model:

```{r f0 acc load model, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
f0peak_acc = readRDS(paste0(parentfolder, "/9_statistical_analysis_scripts_and_model_output/f0peak_acc_new.rds"))
```

### Output

Look at model output and model fit using posterior predictive checks.

```{r f0 acc output, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
f0peak_acc_pp <- pp_check(f0peak_acc, ndraws = 1000)

# This is the model output
f0peak_acc

# These are the posterior predictive checks with 1000 samples.
f0peak_acc_pp

#ggsave(file.path(plots, "f0peak_acc_pp.pdf"), plot = f0peak_acc_pp, width = 7, height = 4)

```

We see strong effect of speech rate and sex. Female sex and faster speech rate go hand in hand with increased F0.

The fit is not ideal, since it includes an additional "bump." **Please see supplementary info for more information.**

Now we run some diagnostics.

```{r f0 acc diagnostics, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE}
mcmc_plot(f0peak_acc, type="hist")

# Please uncomment and run this if you want to see the shinystan GUI and explore the model.
# shiny_f0peak_acc <- launch_shinystan(f0peak_acc)
```

Compute posterior probability of all predictors.

```{r f0 acc posterior probabilities, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE}
posteriors_f0acc <- posterior_samples(f0peak_acc)
sum(posteriors_f0acc$b_speech_rate_s > 0) / nrow(posteriors_f0acc) # 0.9907187
sum(posteriors_f0acc$b_point_direct_s < 0) / nrow(posteriors_f0acc) # 0.9185
sum(posteriors_f0acc$b_wrist_apeak < 0) / nrow(posteriors_f0acc) # 0.8389062
sum(posteriors_f0acc$b_sex_s > 0) / nrow(posteriors_f0acc) # 1
sum(posteriors_f0acc[,6] > 0) / nrow(posteriors_f0acc) # interaction 0.7950312
```

## F0 Deceleration

### Preparation

Check for normality of the outcome variable: F0 peak nearest to deceleration peak.

```{r f0 dec normality, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# This distribution, especially the red line will be the one we will later see in the posterior predictive checks as y
hist(f0_dec$wrist_f0peak_dec, freq = FALSE, main = "Density curve")
lines(density(na.omit(f0_dec$wrist_f0peak_dec)), lwd = 2, col = 'red')

qqnorm(f0_dec$wrist_f0peak_dec)
qqline(f0_dec$wrist_f0peak_dec)

shapiro.test(f0_dec$wrist_f0peak_dec)

ks.test(f0_dec$wrist_f0peak_dec, 'pnorm')
```

The outcome variable is not normally distributed.

Now, let's check for correlation between speech rate and wrist deceleration peak. We use two methods: Bayesian and frequentist.

```{r f0 dec correlations, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Bayes factor
f0dec_corr_s <- correlationBF(f0_dec$speech_rate_s, f0_dec$wrist_decpeak)
describe_posterior(f0dec_corr_s)
bayesfactor(f0dec_corr_s)

# Frequentist Kendall
cor(f0_dec$speech_rate_s, f0_dec$wrist_decpeak)
cor.test(f0_dec$speech_rate_s, f0_dec$wrist_decpeak,  method="kendall")

```

Bayes factor points to a very strong evidence for a correlation.

We set weakly informative priors. Like with acceleration, we truncate the intercept prior to include only positive values, with the lowest point to be 70 Hz. Any lower values would be erroneous octave jumps and they were discarded in the pre-processing.

```{r f0 dec priors, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE,message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
get_prior(
  wrist_f0peak_dec ~ 1 +
    speech_rate_s +
    point_direct_s +
    wrist_decpeak +
    sex_s +
    point_direct_s * wrist_decpeak +
    (1 | speaker) +
    (0 + speech_rate_s + point_direct_s + wrist_decpeak + point_direct_s * wrist_decpeak | speaker) +
    (1 | rhyme) +
    (0 + speech_rate_s + point_direct_s + wrist_decpeak + sex_s + point_direct_s * wrist_decpeak | rhyme),
  data = f0_dec,
  family = "gaussian"
)

prior1 <- set_prior("truncated_normal(0, 200, lower = 70)", class = "Intercept")
prior2 <- set_prior("normal(0, 75)", class = "b", coef = "sex_s")
prior3 <- set_prior("normal(0, 10)", class = "b", coef = "point_direct_s")
prior4 <- set_prior("normal(0, 1)", class = "b", coef = "point_direct_s:wrist_decpeak")
prior5 <- set_prior("normal(0, 10)", class = "b", coef = "speech_rate_s")
prior6 <- set_prior("normal(0, 1)", class = "b", coef = "wrist_decpeak")
prior7 <- set_prior("normal(0, 100)", class = "sd")
prior8 <- set_prior("normal(0, 100)", class = "sigma")
prior9 <- set_prior("lkj(2)", class = "cor")
priors_f0_dec <- list(prior1, prior2, prior3, prior4, prior5, prior6, prior7, prior8, prior9)
priors_f0_dec <- prior_summary(priors_f0_dec)


```

### Gaussian + priors

This is the model code.

```{r f0 dec model, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

f0peak_dec <- brm(
  wrist_f0peak_dec ~ 1 +
    speech_rate_s +
    point_direct_s +
    wrist_decpeak +
    sex_s +
    point_direct_s * wrist_decpeak +
    (1 | speaker) +
    (0 + speech_rate_s + point_direct_s + wrist_decpeak + point_direct_s * wrist_decpeak || speaker) +
    (1 | rhyme) +
    (0 + speech_rate_s + point_direct_s + wrist_decpeak + sex_s + point_direct_s * wrist_decpeak || rhyme),
  data = f0_dec,
  family = "gaussian",
  prior = priors_f0_dec,
  # Technical stuff
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  # Number of chains
  chains = 4, 
  # Number of iterations per chain
  iter = 10000,
  warmup = 2000,
  # Number of cores to use
  cores = 4,
  # Seed for replicability
  seed = 123,
  # Convergence
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
  # Save here
  file = paste0(parentfolder, "/9_statistical_analysis_scripts_and_model_output/f0peak_dec_new.rds"))

```

Load ready model:

```{r f0 dec load model, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
f0peak_dec = readRDS(paste0(parentfolder, "/9_statistical_analysis_scripts_and_model_output/f0peak_dec_new.rds"))
```

### Output

Look at model output and model fit using posterior predictive checks.

```{r f0 dec output, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
f0peak_dec_pp <- pp_check(f0peak_dec, ndraws = 1000)

# This is the model output
f0peak_dec

# These are the posterior predictive checks with 1000 samples.
f0peak_dec_pp

#ggsave(file.path(plots, "f0peak_dec_pp.pdf"), plot = f0peak_dec_pp, width = 7, height = 4)
```

Here, too. Strong effects of speech rate and sex with the same directionality like in F0 acceleration.


```{r}

plot(conditional_effects(f0peak_dec, effects = "wrist_decpeak"), points = TRUE)

```


The fit is not ideal, since it includes an additional "bump." **Please see supplementary info for more information.**
But we see that the posteriors generally follow the distribution, just like with acceleration.

Now we run some diagnostics.

```{r f0 dec diagnostics, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE}
mcmc_plot(f0peak_dec, type="hist")

# Please uncomment and run this if you want to see the shinystan GUI and explore the model.
# shiny_f0peak_dec <- launch_shinystan(f0peak_dec)
```

Compute posterior probability of all predictors.

```{r f0 dec posterior probabilities, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE}
posteriors_f0dec <- posterior_samples(f0peak_dec)
sum(posteriors_f0dec$b_speech_rate_s > 0) / nrow(posteriors_f0dec) # 0.9784687
sum(posteriors_f0dec$b_point_direct_s < 0) / nrow(posteriors_f0dec) # 0.7204687
sum(posteriors_f0dec$b_wrist_decpeak < 0) / nrow(posteriors_f0dec) # 0.7805937
sum(posteriors_f0dec$b_sex_s > 0) / nrow(posteriors_f0dec) # 0.9999687
sum(posteriors_f0dec[,6] < 0) / nrow(posteriors_f0dec) # interaction 0.8067188
```

## Envelope Acceleration

### Preparation

Check for normality of the outcome variable: amplitude envelope peak nearest to acceleration peak.

```{r env acc normality, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# This distribution, especially the red line will be the one we will later see in the posterior predictive checks as y
hist(env_acc$wrist_envpeak_acc_norm, freq = FALSE, main = "Density curve")
lines(density(na.omit(env_acc$wrist_envpeak_acc_norm)), lwd = 2, col = 'red')

qqnorm(env_acc$wrist_envpeak_acc_norm)
qqline(env_acc$wrist_envpeak_acc_norm)

shapiro.test(env_acc$wrist_envpeak_acc_norm) # the data is not normally distributed

ks.test(env_acc$wrist_envpeak_acc_norm, 'pnorm') # also not normally distributed

```

The outcome variable is not normally distributed.

We also check the correlations, like above.

```{r env acc correlations, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Bayes factor
envacc_corr_s <- correlationBF(env_acc$speech_rate_s, env_acc$wrist_apeak)
describe_posterior(envacc_corr_s)
bayesfactor(envacc_corr_s)

# Frequentist Kendall
cor(env_acc$speech_rate_s, env_acc$wrist_apeak)
cor.test(env_acc$speech_rate_s, env_acc$wrist_apeak, method = "kendall")

```

Bayes factor points to a very strong evidence for a correlation.

We set weakly informative priors. We truncate the intercept prior to include only positive values, with the lowest point to be 0. Any lower values would be erroneous and they were discarded in the pre-processing.

```{r env acc priors, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
get_prior(
  wrist_envpeak_acc_norm ~ 1 +
    speech_rate_s +
    point_direct_s +
    wrist_apeak +
    sex_s +
    point_direct_s * wrist_apeak +
    (1 | speaker) +
    (0 + speech_rate_s + point_direct_s + wrist_apeak + point_direct_s * wrist_apeak | speaker) +
    (1 | rhyme) +
    (0 + speech_rate_s + point_direct_s + wrist_apeak + sex_s + point_direct_s * wrist_apeak | rhyme),
  data = env_acc,
  family = "gaussian"
)

prior1 <- set_prior("truncated_normal(0, 5, lower = 0)", class = "Intercept")
prior2 <- set_prior("normal(0, 1)", class = "b", coef = "sex_s")
prior3 <- set_prior("normal(0, 1)", class = "b", coef = "point_direct_s")
prior4 <- set_prior("normal(0, 0.1)", class = "b", coef = "point_direct_s:wrist_apeak")
prior5 <- set_prior("normal(0, 1)", class = "b", coef = "speech_rate_s")
prior6 <- set_prior("normal(0, 0.1)", class = "b", coef = "wrist_apeak")
prior7 <- set_prior("normal(0, 2.5)", class = "sd")
prior8 <- set_prior("normal(0, 2.5)", class = "sigma")
prior9 <- set_prior("lkj(2)", class = "cor")
priors_env_acc <- list(prior1, prior2, prior3, prior4, prior5, prior6, prior7, prior8, prior9)
priors_env_acc <- prior_summary(priors_env_acc)

```

#### Gaussian + priors

This is the model code.

```{r env acc model, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

envpeak_acc <- brm(
  wrist_envpeak_acc_norm ~ 1 +
    speech_rate_s +
    point_direct_s +
    wrist_apeak +
    sex_s +
    point_direct_s * wrist_apeak +
    (1 | speaker) +
    (0 + speech_rate_s + point_direct_s + wrist_apeak + point_direct_s * wrist_apeak || speaker) +
    (1 | rhyme) +
    (0 + speech_rate_s + point_direct_s + wrist_apeak + sex_s + point_direct_s * wrist_apeak || rhyme),
  data = env_acc,
  family = "gaussian",
  prior = priors_env_acc,
  # Technical stuff
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  # Number of chains
  chains = 4, 
  # Number of iterations per chain
  iter = 10000,
  warmup = 2000,
  # Number of cores to use
  cores = 4,
  # Seed for replicability
  seed = 42,
  # Convergence
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.999),
  max_treedepth = 12,
  # Save here
  file = paste0(parentfolder, "/9_statistical_analysis_scripts_and_model_output/envpeak_acc_new.rds"))

```

Load ready model:

```{r env acc load model, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
envpeak_acc = readRDS(paste0(parentfolder, "/9_statistical_analysis_scripts_and_model_output/envpeak_acc_new.rds"))
```

### Output

Look at model output and model fit using posterior predictive checks.

```{r env acc output, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# This is the model output
envpeak_acc

# These are the posterior predictive checks with 1000 samples.
envpeak_acc_pp

#ggsave(file.path(plots, "envpeak_acc_pp.pdf"), plot = envpeak_acc_pp, width = 7, height = 4)

```

The fit is quite good, although there are some instances where y_rep doesn't overlap with y.

```{r}

```


Let's run further diagnostics.


Compute posterior probability of all predictors.

```{r env acc posterior probabilities, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE}

sum(posteriors_mdl_env_acc$b_speech_rate_s < 0) / nrow(posteriors_mdl_env_acc) # 0.8616563
sum(posteriors_mdl_env_acc$b_point_direct_s < 0) / nrow(posteriors_mdl_env_acc) # 0.8878438
sum(posteriors_mdl_env_acc$b_wrist_apeak > 0) / nrow(posteriors_mdl_env_acc) # 0.9010625
sum(posteriors_mdl_env_acc$b_sex_s > 0) / nrow(posteriors_mdl_env_acc) # 0.8140312
```

## Envelope Deceleration

#### Preparation

```{r env dec normality}

ks.test(env_dec$wrist_envpeak_dec_norm, 'pnorm') # also not normally distributed
```

The outcome variable is not normally distributed.

Now, let's check for correlation between speech rate and wrist deceleration peak.


```{r env dec priors, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
prior5 <- set_prior("normal(0, 1)", class = "b", coef = "speech_rate_s")
prior6 <- set_prior("normal(0, 0.1)", class = "b", coef = "wrist_decpeak")
prior7 <- set_prior("normal(0, 2.5)", class = "sd")
prior8 <- set_prior("normal(0, 2.5)", class = "sigma")
prior9 <- set_prior("lkj(2)", class = "cor")
priors_env_dec <- list(prior1, prior2, prior3, prior4, prior5, prior6, prior7, prior8, prior9)
```
